chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Booker Coleman and Tommy Miles bands in Washington, with Jimmy Mundy
summary: He lists his first big-band jobs, Booker Coleman's Hot Chocolates and Tommy Miles, with Elton Hill and Jimmy Mundy, and Eckstine and Tyree Glenn later in the Miles band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: The first band I played in was Booker Coleman's Hot Chocolates around -- this was around Washington, D. C. And I played with Booker Coleman for a while, then I went with Tommy Miles. Tommy Miles Band. Thommy Miles Band had some good musicians in it. Elton Hill was a trumpet player in there, and he was a good arranger. In fact, he arranged some things for Gene Krupa -- Elton Hill -- quite a few things. And Jimmy Mundy was in that band.
I was going to ask you because I noticed that your history and Jimmy Mundy's were rather parallel --
Jimmy Mundy was on that band.
You were with Miles' band, and Elmer Calloway -- were you in the band at the same time?
I was in Elmer Calloway's band. Yeah, you're talking about --
Same time with Jimmy Mundy, right?
Yeah, we were in those bands together.
And then you went on to Earl Hines together?

Yeah. Well, what actually happened was we had such good arrangements in that band and some real good players because eventually Eckstine came on that band, and Tyree Glenn came on that band eventually.
No, No. This was Tommy Miles Band.
Yeah, and we had some very good musicians in that band.
When did -- you were in Tommy Miles' Band in what year?
